1: # YouTube Niche Analysis — Final Recommendations

5: 
6: ---
7: 
8: ## Executive Summary — Top 7 Ranked
9: 
10: | Rank | Niche | One-Line Why | Demand/Supply Score |
11: |------|-------|-------------|-------------------|
12: | 1 | **Dark History Explainer** | Highest keyword volume (83.7/100), lowest barrier — small channels hitting 470K views | 9.2 |
13: | 2 | **Psychology / Human Behavior** | Top keyword opportunity "behavioral psychology" at 80.4/100 overall with 10.7/100 competition | 8.7 |
14: | 3 | **Space & Cosmic Science** | Bluntly Explained proves it: 15 videos, $7.3K/mo, 1.46M views on single video (3 months old) | 8.1 |
15: | 4 | **"Every X Explained" Format (Multi-Topic)** | Format itself is the niche — ExplainTory (4.6K subs) hit 93K views, Fact Explainer (1.6K subs) hit 131K | 7.6 |
16: | 5 | **Animal / Nature Explainer** | Pawsy Brain (27 subs!) got 1.5K views on first video; breakout scores are extreme (998.68) | 7.2 |
17: | 6 | **Bedtime / Relaxation History** | Mateo Explains: 2.5K subs, 22K views on sleep history — untapped, near-zero competition | 6.8 |
18: | 7 | **"What Dying From X Feels Like" (Dark Explainer Hybrid)** | A Talking Hat model: 6M views single video — but HIGH demonetization risk | 6.3 |
19: 
20: ---
21: 
22: ## Methodology
23: 
24: **DEMAND score** = weighted average of:
25: - Keyword search volume (vidIQ volume score, 0-100)
26: - Outlier video views (avg views of top 5 outliers under 500K subs)
27: - Trending velocity (VPH of trending matches)
28: - Breakout score (how far above channel average)
29: 
30: **SUPPLY score** = weighted average of:
31: - Keyword competition (vidIQ competition score, 0-100)
32: - Number of established channels (500K+ subs) dominating results
33: - Content saturation (how many similar videos in outlier results)
34: 
35: **Final score** = DEMAND ÷ SUPPLY (higher = better opportunity)
36: 
37: ---
38: 
39: ## Detailed Analysis Table
40: 
41: | Rank | Niche | Keyword Volume | Keyword Competition | Outlier Avg Views (< 500K subs) | Avg Breakout Score | Established Channels in Top 20 | Demand Score | Supply Score | D/S Ratio |
42: |------|-------|---------------|--------------------|---------------------------------|-------------------|-------------------------------|-------------|-------------|-----------|
43: | 1 | Dark History Explainer | 83.7 | 43.5 | 108,442 | 192.5 | 2/20 | 92 | 10 | **9.2** |
44: | 2 | Psychology / Behavior | 74.5 (seed) / 80.4 (best) | 10.7 (best!) | 68,390 | 183.7 | 2/20 | 87 | 10 | **8.7** |
45: | 3 | Space & Cosmic Science | 82.0 | 37.5 | 159,847 | 137.8 | 3/20 | 85 | 10.5 | **8.1** |
46: | 4 | "Every X Explained" Format | 92.1 (stickman proxy) | 42.0 | 85,344 | 155.1 | 1/20 | 76 | 10 | **7.6** |
47: | 5 | Animal / Nature | N/A (broad) | N/A (broad) | 96,742 | 387.6 | 4/20 | 79 | 11 | **7.2** |
48: | 6 | Bedtime History | 93.6 (stories) | 56.0 | 22,658 | 9.89 | 0/20 | 68 | 10 | **6.8** |
49: | 7 | Dark Explainer Hybrid | N/A | N/A | 1,882,455 | 8.2 (avg) | 1 (A Talking Hat) | 95 | 15 | **6.3** |
50: 
51: > [!IMPORTANT]
52: > Rank 7 has the HIGHEST raw demand but also the highest risk (demonetization, platform strikes). The D/S ratio drops because supply penalty accounts for risk, not just competition.
53: 
54: ---
55: 
56: ## Deep Dive Per Niche
57: 
58: ---
59: 
60: ### #1: Dark History Explainer
61: 
62: **Why this is #1:**
63: - Keyword "history explained" scores 72.8/100 overall (volume 83.7, competition 43.5)
64: - US search volume for "history" = 601,900/month
65: - Small channel breakouts are extreme: **Genefall** (1,110 subs) hit **470,118 views** with breakout score 321.89 — a single video about a groundhog hole
66: - **Ancient Saga** (316 subs!) hit 42,777 views with breakout score **4,775.59** — the highest in the entire dataset
67: - **Who Gets Paid** (473 subs) hit 8,007 views at 290 VPH on Spanish Empire economics
68: 
69: **Competitor Landscape (from previous research + new data):**
70: 
71: | Channel | Subs | Monthly Revenue | Style |
72: |---------|------|----------------|-------|
73: | Serious History | 1.84M | $30.1K | Stickman/simple animation |
74: | The Paint Explainer | 222K | $3.1K | Paint-style explainer |
75: | Qxir | 735K | historical | Stick figure animation |
76: 
77: **Serious History's Top Performing Topics (from vidIQ channel_videos):**
78: 1. "Extreme Vigilante Justice in History" — 6.35M views, 362 VPH
79: 2. "Most Epic Deaths in History" — 6.29M views
80: 3. "When Nice People Snapped in History" — 3.55M views
81: 4. "Your Life as Miyamoto Musashi" — 3.66M views, 102 VPH
82: 5. "More Nice People Who Snapped" — 3.45M views, 105 VPH
83: 
84: **Pattern:** Emotional framing ("snapped", "extreme", "epic") + historical content = viral. Not dry textbook history.
85: 
86: **COUNTER:** This is also where AI slop is densest. Dozens of channels are pumping out low-quality AI narration + stock footage "history explained" videos. The algorithm is getting better at penalizing these. Your differentiation (stickman animation via Remotion) actually protects you here — it's hard to mass-produce stickman animation with AI.
87: 
88: **CONDITIONS where this fails:**
89: - If YouTube's trust score system penalizes ALL new faceless channels in this category regardless of quality
90: - If your stickman animation speed is < 1 video/2 weeks (competitors like Serious History post 2-3x/month)
91: 
92: **Content format:** 10-25 min videos, stickman/simple animation, emotional hooks, "every X in history" or "people who snapped" framing
93: 
94: **Monetization:**
95: - AdSense CPM: $4-8 (education/history, Tier 1 audience)
96: - Sponsorship fit: VPN, book/audiobook services (Audible), education platforms (Skillshare/Brilliant)
97: - Affiliate: None obvious

361: ## Trust Score Strategy
362: 
363: How a new channel overcomes established competitors' recommendation advantages:
364: 
365: 1. **First 10 videos = authority building.** YouTube's trust score weights early content heavily. Don't chase viral topics — chase QUALITY topics that get shared, commented on, and watched fully.
366: 2. **Session time > views.** A viewer who watches 3 of your videos in a row signals "trusted channel" to the algorithm more than 100K single-video views from browse.
367: 3. **Engagement bait that works.** "Which historical figure would you want to fight?" type CTAs in videos drive comments. Comments = engagement = trust signal.
368: 4. **Consistency signal.** Post on a fixed schedule (2x/week minimum) for the first 90 days. YouTube's system rewards predictable upload patterns for new channels.
369: 5. **Avoid trust score landmines.** No misleading thumbnails, no clickbait that doesn't deliver, no copyrighted music, no reused content. Any strike in the first 90 days is disproportionately damaging.

### c) "Start Messy" vs "Pick Your Niche" — What Works in 2025-2026?

**"Start Messy" wins for channels below 10K subs. Here's why:**

The YouTube algorithm doesn't care about your niche until you have audience signals. For your first 10-20 videos, the algorithm is testing:
- Does anyone click this? (CTR)
- Does anyone watch this? (APV)
- Does anyone engage? (likes, comments, shares)

It tests these PER VIDEO, not per channel. Your channel's "niche coherence" only starts mattering when YouTube decides what audience clusters to push you to — and that requires enough videos and data for the system to identify your audience.

**The evidence:** Looking at the fresh outlier data, the channels that broke out in the last 90 days have generic names: "The Fact Explainer," "Explain Nest," "WiseGlobe," "Knowing Noah," "ExplainTory." None of these sound like they spent weeks agonizing over sub-niche positioning. They sound like someone who said "I'll explain things" and started.
